title: Compliance request intake: SLA decision matrix & scoring rubric for logging, retention, and PII controls
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Create a repeatable decision matrix and numeric scoring rubric to triage enterprise requests for logging redaction, retention changes, PII handling, and audit export formats. Goal is to provide consistent SLOs, routing, and acceptance criteria so customer-facing teams can respond within predictable windows and engineers/legal have clear inputs for technical work and risk review.

Why this ticket: We continue to see long, ad-hoc threads for compliance-related asks where severity and required approvals are unclear (e.g., one-off log redaction vs platform-wide retention policy change). The lack of shared scoring leads to misrouted requests, inconsistent SLAs, and engineering rework. This initiative produces a lightweight, numeric rubric + SLA decision matrix, response templates, and routing rules for the intake queue.

Scope:
- Request types: logging redaction, log retention/TTL changes, PII masking/ephemeral keys, audit export formatting and delivery, usage logs deletion/exports.
- Out of scope: production incident triage (bug fixes), billing disputes, model behavior/content requests.

Deliverables:
- A 1-page decision matrix that maps score bands to SLA (acknowledge, initial plan, resolution window) and routing (support -> PM -> security/legal -> infra).
- A 5-point scoring rubric with weightings (customer risk, data sensitivity, required infra change, cross-customer impact, regulatory deadline).
- Triage playbook: intake checklist, artifact requirements (logs sample, customer contract excerpts, compliance deadline), and responder templates.
- Rollout plan for internal teams (Support, SE, Customer Success) and a short training doc.

Acceptance criteria:
- Matrix and rubric finalized and approved by Security and Legal.
- Two pilot requests run through the rubric with time-to-decision tracked and <= 48h acknowledgement SLO met.
- Triaging templates added to Support's playbooks and an internal Confluence page linked from the Console triage flow.

Key trade-offs considered:
- Strict SLA bands speed response but may force conservative decisions that increase infra work. The rubric must allow engineering to flag high-effort requests and recommend alternative mitigations (e.g., customer-side redaction) to avoid over-committing.
- Numeric scoring reduces debate but can obscure qualitative context; we will require a short free-text justification for scores >= 4 in the "data sensitivity" or "regulatory deadline" dimensions.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix approved by Security and Legal
Pilot two real customer requests through the process with tracked timings
Support playbook updated and internal training delivered
SLA targets published: Acknowledge <= 48h, Initial plan <= 7 days, Resolution window defined per score band
steps: Draft scoring rubric and weights (owner: PM)
Workshop with Security/Legal/Infra/Support to validate thresholds
Prototype triage form (Support ticket template) and response templates
Run 2 pilot requests and capture telemetry (timestamps, decisions, follow-ups)
Iterate rubric based on pilot feedback, finalize and publish
Train Support/CS and add links to Console & Confluence
